Performers
Philadelphia Orchestra (orchestra), Leopold Stokowski (conductor) Documented

DAHR gives Philadelphia Orchestra and Leopold Stokowski. The Internet Archive item credits “Philadelphia Symphony Orchestra”, a variant of the same ensemble’s name. DAHR’s instrumentation list (7 first violins, 5 second violins, 3 violas, 2 cellos, 4 basses, harp, 3 oboes, 3 clarinets, 2 bassoons, 2 trumpets, 3 trombones, 2 tubas, traps) comes from Victor ledgers for 15 March 1921 and is not confirmed for the issued take.

[1] [2]
Work version
Abridged orchestral version; which passages are omitted is not documented Inferred, not documented

The abridgement is inferred from the file’s length, 4:06, against a typical performance of 7½–9 minutes (Wikipedia), and from the disc being a single 12-inch side. DAHR and the Internet Archive do not describe the cut, and neither names an edition or cut scheme. This dossier does not locate cut bars.

[1] [3]
Recorded
18 April 1921 (issued take 4); earlier takes 1–⁠2 on 15 March 1921 Documented

DAHR: takes 1 and 2 on 15 March 1921 and 3 on 18 April were destroyed; take 4 (18 April 1921) is the issued master. A bracketed [1921] is the date given for the issue on Victor 74698. Some listings give the earlier date for the first takes.

[1]
Place
Camden, New Jersey Documented

DAHR gives Camden, New Jersey for every take.

[1]
Label
Victor (Red Seal, 12-in. single-faced) Documented

DAHR describes the object as Victor 74698, Red Seal 12-inch single-faced. Later issues on Victor 6366 and Gramophone Company DB-599 and 3-0662 are listed for the same matrix and take.

[2]
Catalogue
Victor 74698 Documented

The Internet Archive item also shows matrix and catalogue number 74698 and publisher “Victrola”.

[2] [3]
Matrix, take, sides
C-24988, take 4 Documented

The Internet Archive item shows 74698 as its matrix number; the Victor matrix is C-24988.

[1]
Transfer
George Blood, L.P. (digitisation (scanning centre), Great 78 Project) Documented

The item metadata names George Blood, L.P. as scanning centre and credits Robert Boggs with metadata and transfer entry and Kevin Coupe with cleaning (as Internet Archive user fields).

[3]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

The item’s public date is 19 March 2021; that is the upload date, not a transfer date.

[3]
Processing
Digitised at 78 rpm with four styli (3.8, 2.3, 2.8 and 3.3 mil truncated conical); the preferred version was selected by an engineer at George Blood and copied to the friendly file name Documented

The item’s notes say the record was acoustic and that the other side was “not completed due to physical condition of disc”. The MP3 used here is the Internet Archive derivative of the 24-bit FLAC; no further processing is disclosed.

[3]
Composition rights
Sibelius died in 1957; in countries with a life-plus-70 term the composition remains in copyright until the end of 2027 Inferred, not documented

Computed from the composer’s life dates, given in DAHR’s MARC record as 1865–⁠1957. The composition’s status in other territories is not assessed. The programme’s rule applies to the sound recording.

[2]
Recording rights
Rule 2 — United States public domain: first published in 1921, before the 1926 cut-off. Documented

DAHR records the issue on Victor 74698 as [1921]; the brackets mean the year was supplied by the cataloguer, and no month of issue is recorded. The take issued was made on 18 April 1921, so publication followed that date. The Internet Archive item date is also 1921. The item has no licence URL and no non-commercial restriction in its metadata.

[1] [2] [3]

Jean Sibelius, Finlandia, Op. 26 No. 7 (abridged). Philadelphia Orchestra, Leopold Stokowski. Victor 74698 (matrix C-24988, take 4), recorded 18 April 1921 in Camden, New Jersey. Transfer by George Blood, L.P. for the Great 78 Project, Internet Archive. Rights statement
